scenario: [LGRA.5.8.6]: JSON text one byte past the text limit, 24,577 bytes, handed to a host parse, is refused with `DS_ERR_JSON_LIMIT` (-221) before any of it is read. Nothing changes, and NO fault event reaches the stream: the status is the whole host refusal. The site is the cache seed ([NSTG.9.1]): `runner.py`'s `_cache_seeds` passes `json.dumps(value)`, which writes U+0001 as the six bytes `\u0001` and separates array items with `, `. The value is LGRA.5.8.6_host_text_at_limit's with its last string `aaaaaa` instead of `aaaaa`: text 24,577 bytes, value inside the three tree limits (depth 2, 3 nodes, 13,404 string bytes), so the text limit is the only one it crosses. `message_contains` names the text limit, so a refusal by any other limit fails this vector. PATH PINNED: on libds, `ds_json_parse`'s `len > DS_JSON_MAX_TEXT_BYTES` test in pyds's `cache_seed`; `ds_engine_cache_seed` is never called. On the Mercury runtime, `test_behave.m` hands `ds.engine.seed_cache_text` the same `json.dumps` text, and `ds.json_text.parse` refuses it on the same byte count.
